result.title: Did the LLM Answer the Question? A Semantic Reconstruction Game for Jailbreak Evaluation
result.summary: Jailbreak attacks against large language models (LLMs) are evaluated using attack success rate (ASR), which depends on correctly identifying responses that fulfill prohibited requests. Existing evaluators can mistake refusals or topically related responses for successful attacks. We show that changing only the judge LLM can alter reported ASR by up to $82$ percentage points. We introduce the semantic reconstruction game, a training-free evaluator that decomposes compliance judgments into constrained semantic comparisons. Given only a response, an LLM reconstructs the request answered by its substantive content, excluding information merely repeated or refused. The game compares this reconstruction against similar decoy requests to determine whether it matches the original request, allowing abstention when neither candidate matches. Across three off-the-shelf LLM judges, the game achieves the lowest mean error against human labels among evaluated methods and reduces variation in reported ASR. It prioritizes avoiding false positives, even at the cost of missing some successful jailbreaks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 LLM 越狱评测中攻击成功率依赖判定器、易把拒答或话题相关回复误判为成功的问题，提出无训练的「语义重构游戏」评估器：只用回复反推其所回应的请求，再与相似干扰请求比较以判断是否匹配原请求，并允许弃权，从而降低误报。
AI.relevance_reason: 其由回复反推请求、与干扰项比对并允弃权的判别思路可能可供核查，用于探测 VLM 答案是否真正使用了给定视觉证据而非语言先验，但属推测性迁移。
